title: Research sets direction, not results
statement: Use published research, judgment-set values and simulated students to direct and stress-test a design, never as proof of whether or how well it works, which only real learners' outcomes show.
detail: The reading course plans' research priorities say their corpus grounds design and does not prove that their implementation works, and is never to be cited as evidence about the courses' outcomes (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/docs/reading-science/PRIORITIES.qmd`); their quality standard adds that synthetic prediction, benchmark scores and approval on review are not outcome evidence (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/docs/standards/course-quality.qmd`). After an assessment's baseline from a biased slice was replaced by the full population's 196.0, the 46th percentile (n=915), its approval case was held to direction, not magnitude, with no growth number before its pilot (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/docs/course-formula-agents.md`), and an audit relabelled a simulation presented as agreement with the real test as internal cross-bank consistency (synthetic) (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/validity/00_AUDITS_AND_FIXES.md`). A video BrainLift tags each rule as learning evidence, an accessibility requirement, a platform constraint or an operating heuristic, never cites a heuristic as a proven threshold, cites conservative independent numbers because effect sizes inflate when a principle's originator is an author, and lets its own delayed-recall data overrule a cited effect (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g7-science/brainlifts/video-generation-agent-v0.2.md`, `grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g7-science/brainlifts/video-generation-human-v0.2.md`). Tag every rule with its evidence. Research and simulation give neither the size of an effect nor a prediction of an outside score.
against: the same engine found a real structural cliff in a course design, so a simulation is useful for finding structure, not size. Later, 409 real external test records for 173 students turned up, blocked only by an ID crosswalk (`grade3-reading/artifacts/wiki-research/pedagogy-llm-evals.md`). Scripted walks still play a lesson as a student, to catch defects in its flow rather than to measure learning (`grade3-reading/artifacts/team-direction-2026-09-09/GATE-STANDARD-DRAFT.md`). self-reported simulation over about 17,900 sessions gave ability recovery of r = 0.967 and reliability of 0.931, which is simulation rather than a link to real scores (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0086-round2-feedback-brainlifts-2026-07-09.qmd`, line 39). The same summary reports that a model asked to predict where students will struggle, instead of acting as a student, does better: "Teacher-as-predictor instead reaches r ≈ 0.72–0.79 population-level prediction across three independent research groups" (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0007-ti-courseplans-repo.qmd`, line 75). the 67% and r≈0.72–0.79 figures are cited second-hand in the notes, without a DOI or URL, and the notes were written while there was no real-student data to calibrate against (`ti-courseplans-audit/docs/generator-insights.md`).
